candidates.name: WinHttpOpen
verified_facts: Creates a WinHTTP session handle and defines the session-level access type, proxy mode, and asynchronous behavior.
semantic_limits: A session handle only establishes WinHTTP configuration state; it does not prove endpoint reachability, TLS trust, response identity, or receipt production.

candidates.name: WinHttpConnect
verified_facts: Specifies an initial target server and port for a WinHTTP session and returns a connection handle.
semantic_limits: A connection handle is a logical request context and does not prove that a TCP or TLS connection has been established.

candidates.name: WinHttpOpenRequest
verified_facts: Creates a request handle with a method, object path, HTTP version, referrer, accepted types, and security flags.
semantic_limits: Opening a request does not transmit bytes or validate the server, URL, response, or process that will use the handle.

candidates.name: WinHttpSendRequest
verified_facts: Sends request headers and optional request data for a WinHTTP request handle.
semantic_limits: A successful send only confirms WinHTTP accepted the operation; redirects, authentication, proxying, and later failures still require readback.

candidates.name: WinHttpReceiveResponse
verified_facts: Completes a request and makes the status code and response headers available for inspection.
semantic_limits: Successful receipt of headers does not prove the body is complete, semantically valid, from the expected process, or tied to the canonical task.

candidates.name: WinHttpQueryHeaders
verified_facts: Retrieves raw or parsed request and response header values from a WinHTTP request handle.
semantic_limits: Headers are peer-provided metadata and must not substitute for body digest, TLS chain, socket, process, task, and time correlation.

candidates.name: WinHttpQueryHeadersEx
verified_facts: Retrieves parsed header names and values with index and buffer accounting for a request handle.
semantic_limits: Parsed headers can be duplicated, reordered, truncated by buffers, or untrusted; exact raw evidence and status must be retained.

candidates.name: WinHttpQueryDataAvailable
verified_facts: Reports the number of response-body bytes currently available for a subsequent read.
semantic_limits: Available-byte counts are transient and do not equal total content length or prove that the remaining response will arrive.

candidates.name: WinHttpReadData
verified_facts: Reads response body bytes from a WinHTTP request handle into an application buffer.
semantic_limits: Individual reads can be partial; acceptance requires ordered accumulation, exact byte count, end-of-stream, digest, and error-status readback.

candidates.name: WinHttpReadDataEx
verified_facts: Reads response data with extended completion and buffer behavior for a request handle.
semantic_limits: Extended reads remain partial asynchronous observations and do not establish complete or trusted response content.

candidates.name: WinHttpWriteData
verified_facts: Writes request-body bytes to a WinHTTP request after request setup.
semantic_limits: Writing bytes mutates a remote request stream and was not performed here; the documentation is used only to define lifecycle boundaries.

candidates.name: WinHttpSetTimeouts
verified_facts: Sets resolve, connect, send, and receive timeout values on a WinHTTP session or request.
semantic_limits: Timeout configuration does not guarantee enforcement at every layer and does not prove whether an observed delay is network, proxy, TLS, server, or process related.

candidates.name: WinHttpSetOption
verified_facts: Sets a supported WinHTTP option on a session, connection, or request handle.
semantic_limits: Option mutation was not performed; option state must be queried on the exact handle and cannot be inferred from defaults or documentation.

candidates.name: WinHttpQueryOption
verified_facts: Queries supported WinHTTP handle properties such as URLs, security flags, certificates, proxy, or connection information.
semantic_limits: Queried options are handle-scoped snapshots and require exact handle hierarchy, lifecycle, process, and observation-time correlation.

candidates.name: WinHttpCloseHandle
verified_facts: Closes a WinHTTP session, connection, or request handle and initiates resource cleanup.
semantic_limits: Handle closure does not prove all asynchronous callbacks completed, all response bytes were consumed, or task output was committed.

candidates.name: WinHttpSetStatusCallback
verified_facts: Registers a callback for selected WinHTTP status notifications on a handle.
semantic_limits: Callbacks can be asynchronous, reordered, or omitted by selected flags; callback presence alone is not complete request evidence.

candidates.name: WINHTTP_STATUS_CALLBACK
verified_facts: Defines callback parameters for WinHTTP handle, status, context, and status-specific information.
semantic_limits: Callback data is transient and pointer lifetimes are status-specific; it must be copied safely and joined to the exact handle and request.
